Day 1 15 February 2027 · Monday

Arrival in the Island

Colombo Airport (BIA) — Kotugoda

Your Sri Lankan journey begins with a warm welcome at Bandaranaike International Airport, where our representative meets you and escorts you to your waiting vehicle. From here it is only a short, comfortable transfer to Kotugoda, a peaceful pocket of the western coastal belt set among coconut plantations and paddy land — an ideal first footfall for travellers arriving from a long-haul flight.

You check in to The Wallawwa, a beautifully restored colonial-era manor house cradled by landscaped gardens, and the remainder of the day is entirely at leisure. Unwind in your suite, wander the shaded grounds or simply relax by the pool as you settle into the island's gentle pace and warm climate. This restful first night is designed to let you recover fully, so the touring days ahead begin refreshed.

Your Stay

The Wallawwa

15 – 16 Feb 2027  ·  Garden Suite  ·  Bed & Breakfast

A gracefully restored colonial-era manor house set within lush landscaped gardens, The Wallawwa is a serene sanctuary just minutes from the airport yet a world away from it. Shaded verandas, a spa pavilion and a canopy of mature trees frame a property that has become a byword for a gentle, restorative arrival in Sri Lanka. Contemporary comforts sit lightly within the heritage architecture, and the celebrated cuisine and tranquil pool make it the ideal place to shake off a long-haul flight before the touring begins.

Day 2 16 February 2027 · Tuesday

Into the Cultural Triangle

Kotugoda — Thirappane

After breakfast you leave the coastal belt behind and travel north into the heart of Sri Lanka's Cultural Triangle. The drive carries you through a shifting landscape of paddy fields, village tanks and dry-zone scrub, an early and evocative sense of the rural rhythms that define this part of the island.

Your home for the coming nights is Ulagalla, an estate resort of paddy land, lakes and woodland surrounding a restored 150-year-old manor house, where secluded pool villas lie scattered across the grounds. In the evening you gather for the resort's signature Kamatha dinner — staged on a traditional threshing floor, the working heart of the old paddy village — for an atmospheric open-air feast beneath the stars, and a memorable introduction to the culture and cuisine of the dry zone.

Ulagalla

Ulagalla is an award-winning resort woven around a 150-year-old restored manor house at the centre of a vast private estate of paddy land, lakes and woodland. Its individual pool villas are spread generously across the grounds, each a private retreat with its own plunge pool and uninterrupted views across the tank and fields. The estate is alive with birdlife and rural rhythm, and its signature open-air Kamatha dinner, staged on a traditional threshing floor beneath the stars, is one of the most atmospheric dining experiences in the dry zone.

Day 3 17 February 2027 · Wednesday

Wilderness of the Villus

Thirappane — Wilpattu — Thirappane

An early start takes you to Wilpattu National Park, the largest and oldest of Sri Lanka's national parks, named for the villus — natural sand-rimmed rainwater lakes scattered through the forest that draw wildlife out of the surrounding scrub and make for exceptional viewing. You explore in an open safari vehicle with an experienced tracker, moving between the villus where the cool morning hours are most rewarding.

Wilpattu is among the finest places in the country to search for the elusive Sri Lankan leopard, and it also shelters elephant, sloth bear, spotted deer, sambar, buffalo, crocodile and a remarkable variety of birdlife. Compared with the island's busier parks it retains a wonderfully wild, uncrowded character. After the safari you return to Ulagalla, where the evening is yours — to relax in your pool villa or watch the sunset settle over the paddy fields.

Day 4 18 February 2027 · Thursday

The Estate at Leisure

Thirappane — Ulagalla Estate

Today is given to the Ulagalla estate itself. The morning unfolds at your own pace among the resort's in-house experiences — discovering the grounds, learning about the estate's heritage and working paddy land, or simply enjoying the setting in comfort, connected to the traditional life of the dry zone.

In the late afternoon you set out on the Ulagalla scenic drive, a guided exploration timed to coincide with sunset. The route crosses the property's varied terrain — past paddy fields, along the tank bunds and through pockets of woodland — with fine opportunities to observe resident birdlife. As the light softens, the drive culminates in sundowners, the sky mirrored in the water of the tank and the paddy turning to gold: a peaceful, photogenic close to a relaxed day.

Day 5 19 February 2027 · Friday

The First Great Capital

Thirappane — Anuradhapura — Thirappane

This morning you travel the short distance to Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka's first great capital. Founded in the fourth century BC and the seat of power for over a thousand years, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most significant sacred cities in the Buddhist world, sprawling across a vast landscape of ruins, reservoirs and living shrines.

Among its treasures stand the colossal brick dagobas of Ruwanwelisaya, Jetavanaramaya and Abhayagiri — once among the tallest structures on earth — alongside monastic complexes, bathing ponds and exquisitely carved moonstones. At its heart is the Sri Maha Bodhi, grown from a cutting of the tree beneath which the Buddha attained enlightenment and revered as the oldest historically documented tree in the world. Later, a gentle kayaking experience on the region's calm tank waters lets you appreciate this ancient hydraulic landscape from water level, birdlife all around, before you return to Ulagalla.

◷Sacred-city tour & kayaking✦Bed & Breakfast

Day 6 20 February 2027 · Saturday

The Gathering

Thirappane — Sigiriya — Minneriya — Sigiriya

After breakfast you check out and transfer to Sigiriya, travelling deeper into the Cultural Triangle through tanks, scrub jungle and scattered rock outcrops. On arrival you check in to Water Garden Sigiriya, where villas sit among landscaped water channels and lily ponds, with the great rock rising dramatically above the treeline.

In the afternoon you set out on a jeep safari in Minneriya National Park, built around a reservoir constructed by King Mahasen in the third century AD and one of the finest places in Asia to observe wild elephant. As the dry season advances, elephants converge on the receding shoreline to feed on fresh grasses — a seasonal congregation known as The Gathering, which can bring together great numbers in a single open grassland and ranks among the region's finest wildlife spectacles. Watch too for spotted deer, buffalo, macaques and waterbirds including painted storks and pelicans.

Day 7 21 February 2027 · Sunday

The Lion Rock

Sigiriya Rock Fortress

This morning you visit Sigiriya Rock Fortress, the most iconic monument in Sri Lanka and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Rising some 200 metres sheer from the plain, this vast granite monolith was transformed in the fifth century AD by King Kasyapa into a royal citadel of extraordinary ambition — part palace, part fortress, and one of the earliest examples of landscape urban planning in the world.

The approach leads through symmetrical water, boulder and terraced gardens whose fountains still function during the rains. A spiral stairway climbs to the sheltered gallery of the celebrated frescoes, their colour intact after fifteen centuries, and on past the Mirror Wall to the enormous carved paws of the Lion Staircase that gave the rock its name. The final ascent emerges onto the summit, where the foundations of Kasyapa's palace command a breathtaking panorama across the jungle to the horizon. The evening is at leisure at the resort.

Day 8 22 February 2027 · Monday

Into the Wild East

Sigiriya — Gal Oya

After breakfast you depart Sigiriya and travel southeast to Gal Oya, one of the least visited and most rewarding corners of the island. The journey passes through changing country as the Cultural Triangle gives way to the wild, sparsely populated interior of the east, forested hills and open scrub replacing the ancient tanks and monuments of previous days.

On arrival you check in to Gal Oya Lodge, a pioneering eco-lodge on a private estate at the edge of the national park, at the foot of a striking granite outcrop. The remainder of the day is at leisure to settle in and absorb the extraordinary quiet — a place that rewards stillness, alive with birdlife and butterflies by day and offering superb star-gazing by night, with almost no light pollution for many kilometres in any direction.

Day 9 23 February 2027 · Tuesday

Elephants of the Lake

Gal Oya National Park

Today is devoted to Gal Oya National Park, and it begins on the water. Gal Oya Lake — formed by the Senanayake Samudraya, the largest water body in Sri Lanka — provides a stunning setting for a boat safari through an almost Jurassic landscape of forested islands and drowned hills. Gal Oya is celebrated as the one place in the country where elephants are known to swim between the islands, and the boat offers the rare privilege of watching wildlife from the water rather than the road.

Later you head back into the park with a resident naturalist for a jungle drive into the forgotten Nilgala section, prized for its medicinal plants and its mosaic of savannah grassland, riverine forest and rocky outcrops. The naturalist's presence brings real depth to the day, drawing out the ecology, the plant lore and the subtle signs of wildlife — elephant, deer and abundant birdlife — that would otherwise pass unnoticed.

Day 10 24 February 2027 · Wednesday

Climbing to the Hills

Gal Oya — Ella

This morning you leave the eastern lowlands behind and climb into the hill country, transferring to Ella — a small town wrapped in tea gardens, cloud forest and dramatic mountain scenery, and one of the most beloved destinations in Sri Lanka. The road gains altitude steadily and the landscape is transformed: the hot, open scrub of the east gives way to steep green slopes, neatly contoured tea bushes, misted ridgelines and a welcome coolness in the air.

On arrival you check in to Uga Ghiri, set amid the tranquillity of the surrounding highlands, and the remainder of the day is entirely at leisure. Settle into your villa, breathe the clean mountain air and take in the sweeping views across the hills, or simply relax and let the pace slow after the long journey from the east. It is a gentle first evening in the highlands, with nothing to do but enjoy the cool and the calm.

Day 11 25 February 2027 · Thursday

The Pekoe Trail

Ella — Tea Country & Little Adam's Peak

This morning you walk Stage 16 of the Pekoe Trail, part of the celebrated long-distance route that threads through Sri Lanka's central highlands along old plantation paths and colonial-era tracks. Walking here brings you close to the rhythms of estate life in a way no vehicle can — the contoured tea bushes climbing the slopes, the pluckers at work among them, and the factories that have shaped this landscape since the British planted the first highland tea in the nineteenth century — with sweeping views across the valleys and ridgelines of the Ella region.

Later you head to Little Adam's Peak for the Ravana adventure experiences. Named for its resemblance in profile to the sacred Adam's Peak further west, the hill rises above the Ella Gap, and its slopes host a cluster of activities that make the most of the dramatic terrain and the extraordinary views towards the southern plains. The setting takes its name from the legend of King Ravana, the demon king of the Ramayana, whose story is woven through the caves, waterfalls and peaks of the region.

Day 12 26 February 2027 · Friday

The Hill Station

Ella — Town Tour & Leisure

This morning you enjoy an Ella town tour, exploring the characterful centre of this much-loved hill station. Ella is little more than a single relaxed main street of cafés, small shops and craft stalls set against a backdrop of mountains, and the tour takes in its easy-going, unhurried atmosphere. The town sits at the head of the celebrated Ella Gap, a dramatic cleft that opens southwards towards the distant plains, with neatly contoured tea bushes covering the slopes on every side.

The remainder of the day is at leisure at Uga Ghiri. Spend the afternoon exactly as you wish — relaxing in the cool highland air, taking in the far-reaching views across the tea country, or simply unwinding in the calm of the resort before your journey continues. It is a restful close to your time in the hills, and a fitting pause before the descent to the southern plains.

Day 13 27 February 2027 · Saturday

Descent to Leopard Country

Ella — Yala

After breakfast you begin the descent from the hill country to the southeastern plains, a scenic journey from cool tea slopes down through changing vegetation to the hot, open dry zone of the deep south. On arrival you check in to Hilton Yala Resort, set close to the park boundary with the Indian Ocean nearby.

In the afternoon you set out on a jeep safari in Yala National Park, the most famous wildlife reserve in Sri Lanka. Its landscape is a compelling mix of open scrub, monsoon forest, brackish lagoons, rocky outcrops and coastal dunes, supporting an exceptional density of wildlife. Yala is renowned above all for its leopards — widely regarded as one of the best places on earth to see the cat in the wild — while elephant, sloth bear, deer, crocodile and troops of langur roam alongside a spectacular array of birdlife. The drive continues until the park closes at dusk.

Day 14 28 February 2027 · Sunday

Dawn in Yala

Yala National Park

An early start takes you back into Yala for a further jeep safari, entering the park at dawn when wildlife activity peaks and the light is at its most beautiful. The cool hours immediately after sunrise are the most productive of the day: leopards are frequently on the move, elephants come to the waterholes to drink, and the forest and scrub come alive with birdsong.

A second drive is invaluable, allowing your tracker to work different sectors and follow up on the previous day's sightings. Each safari in Yala is different, shaped by the season, the water levels and the movements of the animals themselves, and the variety of habitat carries you from open plains to dense thicket to lagoon shore within a single morning. After the safari you return to the resort, where the evening is at leisure to relax and reflect on your time in the wild.

Day 15 1 March 2027 · Monday

To the Golden Coast

Yala — Tangalle

After breakfast you leave the dry-zone wilderness of Yala and travel west along the southern coast to Tangalle, exchanging safari jeeps and scrub jungle for palm-fringed sand and the open Indian Ocean. The drive follows the coastal belt through fishing villages, paddy land and coconut groves, with glimpses of everyday life in the deep south.

On arrival you check in to Anantara Peace Haven Tangalle, set on a headland above a private stretch of golden beach and surrounded by an established coconut plantation — a secluded promontory with the ocean on two sides. Tangalle occupies one of the least developed and most beautiful stretches of Sri Lanka's coastline, where wide bays and rocky headlands alternate and life remains unhurried. This is the restful conclusion to your journey, and the rest of the day is yours: settle in, enjoy the beach, or watch the sun set over the ocean from the headland.

Days by the Ocean

Tangalle — At Leisure

These four days are yours entirely, set aside for rest on one of the most beautiful stretches of coastline in Sri Lanka. After an active, varied journey through the Cultural Triangle, the eastern wilderness, the hill country and the southern parks, this is the moment to slow down completely and enjoy the ocean at your own pace, with no fixed programme to keep.

Anantara Peace Haven occupies a secluded headland above a private beach, framed by a mature coconut plantation and open to the sea on two sides. Spend your time exactly as you wish — long mornings by the pool, unhurried meals, quiet hours on the sand, or watching the fishing boats work the bay and the sun set over the water each evening. For the more active, the resort offers in-house activities such as snorkelling and games, arranged directly with the resort at your convenience (these are payable locally and are not included in the tour price). It is a fitting, restorative interlude before the final leg.

Day 20 6 March 2027 · Saturday

The Capital by the Sea

Tangalle — Colombo

After a final leisurely breakfast overlooking the ocean, you check out and transfer to Colombo, travelling north along the southern coast and up the western seaboard to Sri Lanka's vibrant commercial capital. The journey traces the shoreline for much of its length, ocean on one side and a succession of coastal towns, fishing harbours and coconut groves on the other.

On arrival you check in to the Shangri-La Colombo, on the seafront at Galle Face with commanding views over the Indian Ocean and the city skyline. Its central position places the historic Fort district, the colonial-era landmarks and the open expanse of Galle Face Green — where the city gathers each evening to walk the promenade at sunset — within easy reach. The remainder of the day is at leisure to enjoy the hotel or take the city gently as your journey draws towards its close.

Day 21 7 March 2027 · Sunday

Until Next Time

Colombo — Colombo Airport (BIA)

Your Sri Lankan journey comes to a close today. After breakfast at the Shangri-La and a final opportunity to enjoy the ocean views, you check out at the appropriate time and transfer to Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake, comfortably in advance of your departure flight. Our representative assists you at the airport and sees you safely on your way.

You depart having travelled the length and breadth of this remarkable island — from the ancient dagobas of Anuradhapura and the summit of Sigiriya, through the wild waters of Gal Oya, up into the tea-covered highlands of Ella, out onto the leopard plains of Yala and finally to the golden shores of Tangalle. It is a journey that takes in the very best of Sri Lanka's history, wildlife, landscape and hospitality — and we hope it is the first of many visits.
